_request.system:
You classify a single ERP requirement into exactly one of four delivery tiers, using only the SAP standard-process knowledge entries provided to you.

  Fit           The delivered standard already does this once baseline org structures exist.
  Configuration The delivered logic does this, driven by values maintained in customizing                 (thresholds, code lists, org units, number ranges, determination rules). No code.
  Enhancement   The standard process still drives the flow, but a delivered object must carry an                 extra custom field, or extra logic must run at a published extension point.
  Development   The standard provides no object, no process, and no extension point covering the                 request; a new program, interface, or persistence must be built and maintained.

Method:
- Reason from the knowledge entries' stated boundaries: what the standard covers, what is a   configuration point, and what is stated to be beyond the standard.
- Do NOT classify from surface features. "It mentions an external system" is not a reason.   The reason must be that the standard provides no object, process, or extension point for it,   and that the transport, mapping, scheduling, and error handling are project deliverables.
- A requirement to make an already-delivered field required is field-status configuration.   A requirement to enforce entry in a field the delivered object does not have, or to gate a   process on a condition the standard data model does not carry, is an enhancement.
- In rationale, cite the specific entry IDs whose boundary decided the call, and say what that   boundary is. Cite only entries you were given.
- Set confidence below 0.7 when the entries conflict or none of them squarely covers the request.
_request.user:
Requirement (master_data): Product master data must be created with material type, base unit, product group, plant views, and valuation data before open orders are migrated.

Verbatim from the workshop: "product master data has to be created with material type, base unit, product group, plant views, and valuation data before open orders are migrated"

Knowledge entries retrieved for this requirement:

### KB-MD-004 — Product master standard views [master_data]
Standard process: The product master is organized as a set of views layered over organizational levels. Client-level data carries the product number, product type, base unit of measure, product group, weights, and dimensions. Plant-level views carry planning, procurement, and quality attributes. Valuation views carry the price control indicator, the valuation class, and the standard or moving average price. Sales and storage views carry the remaining organizational attributes. Creating a product with product type, base unit, product group, plant views, and valuation views is delivered behaviour and requires only that the organizational levels exist.
Capabilities covered by the standard: Client-level attributes including product type, base unit, product group, and old product number.; Plant-level views for planning, procurement, and quality management.; Valuation views with price control, valuation class, and price.; Language-dependent product descriptions and alternative units of measure.
Common configuration points: Product types and the views they permit.; Number ranges per product type, internal or external.; Field selection per product type, plant, and transaction.; Valuation classes and their account determination.
Typically beyond the standard: Attributes that no delivered view carries, such as project-specific handling classifications.; Attaching externally sourced documents to products in bulk according to a project's linkage rules.

### KB-MD-005 — Extending master data objects with custom fields and checks [master_data]
Standard process: Master data objects expose extension points for adding custom fields and for running logic when a record is saved. A requirement to track an attribute the delivered object does not carry, and then to warn or block a downstream process when that attribute has a particular state, is met by adding the field and placing the check at an extension point. The delivered maintenance process, its authorizations, and its change documents continue to work. This is materially different from configuration, because a table entry cannot create a field that does not exist, and materially different from custom development, because no new object or interface is created.
Capabilities covered by the standard: Custom fields can be added to business partner and product master and surfaced on the maintenance user interface.; Save-time and check-time extension points run project logic.; Custom fields can be exposed on released APIs, in analytics, and in change documents.; Delivered classification allows attributes to be attached without changing the object.
Common configuration points: Field status for delivered fields per role, grouping, or type.; Classification: class types, characteristics, and allowed values.
Typically beyond the standard: Warning or blocking a transaction based on the expiry state of a certificate the object does not deliver a field for.; Checks that depend on data held only in an application outside the ERP system.; Cross-object checks whose trigger is not modelled in the delivered data model.

### KB-MD-001 — Business partner master for suppliers and customers [master_data]
Standard process: Suppliers and customers are maintained as business partners. A business partner carries general data such as names, addresses, communication data, tax numbers, and bank details, and it takes on roles that add role-specific views. The supplier role adds company code data such as reconciliation account and payment terms, and purchasing organization data such as order currency and incoterms. The customer role adds sales area data. Creating a supplier with name, address, tax number, bank details, and purchasing data is entirely delivered behaviour; the fields exist on the delivered object and the maintenance transaction ships with the product.
Capabilities covered by the standard: General data: names, multiple time-dependent addresses, tax numbers by tax type, bank details.; Roles that switch on supplier, customer, and financial services views.; Company code and purchasing organization segments for suppliers.; Central blocking and deletion indicators, and duplicate check during creation.
Common configuration points: Business partner groupings and their number ranges.; Business partner roles permitted per grouping.; Field status per role and per grouping.; Account groups and reconciliation account determination.
Typically beyond the standard: Attributes the delivered partner object does not carry, such as project-specific scores or certificate registries.; Loading partner attributes on a schedule from an application outside the ERP system.

### KB-MD-002 — Number ranges and groupings for master data [master_data]
Standard process: Master data objects draw their keys from number range intervals. An interval is either internal, meaning the system assigns the next number, or external, meaning the user or a loading program supplies the key. Intervals are assigned to a grouping or type, so different categories of the same object can be numbered separately. When a new legal entity is stood up, giving it its own intervals so that its records do not collide with those of the parent is a matter of defining intervals and assigning them to the relevant groupings. This is customizing content and needs no code.
Capabilities covered by the standard: Internal and external number assignment per object.; Multiple intervals per object, assigned by grouping, account group, or type.; Buffering and gap behaviour for high-volume assignment.
Common configuration points: Number range object intervals, including from-number, to-number, and external flag.; Assignment of intervals to business partner groupings, material types, and document types.; Separate intervals per company code or per organizational unit where the object supports it.
Typically beyond the standard: Key formats that encode business meaning the number range object cannot express.; Renumbering existing records while preserving references, which is a migration build.

parsed.rationale: Standard process KB-MD-004 states: 'Creating a product with product type, base unit, product group, plant views, and valuation views is delivered behaviour and requires only that the organizational levels exist.' Thus, the requirement is covered by the standard without configuration or enhancement.
